What It Is: Companies Act Compliance is the governance arrangements, decision rights, approvals and records that direct and oversee the organization. Within Corporate Governance Compliance, it defines the obligation, accountable roles, control activities and evidence needed to demonstrate conformity.
Why It Is Important: It protects accountability, lawful decision-making, shareholder interests and reliable oversight, and prevents unauthorized commitments or management override.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed to meet company law, governance codes, constitutional documents, board mandates and stakeholder expectations. Primary catalogue basis: ISO 37000; G20/OECD Principles; King IV. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Maintain approved governance bodies, charters, authority limits, meeting calendars, disclosures and decision records; route matters through authorized review and preserve an auditable trail. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Define applicable governance rules; assign board/management accountability; maintain approved charters and authority matrices; schedule required meetings and filings; declare conflicts; document decisions; monitor overdue actions and exceptions. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Approved charters, board/committee papers, agendas, minutes, resolutions, registers, declarations, authority approvals, filings and action-closure records. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when required governance actions occurred on time, by authorized persons, with complete approvals and records, and no unresolved mandatory governance breach remains. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes missing or late meetings/filings, unauthorized approval, undisclosed conflicts, incomplete statutory records, invalid delegations or unsupported decisions.
Typical Applicability / SBU: All legal entities and corporate offices

What It Is: Annual General Meeting (AGM) is the controlled preparation, review, approval, submission and retention of a mandatory filing, return, disclosure, register or formal record. Within Corporate Governance Compliance, it defines the obligation, accountable roles, control activities and evidence needed to demonstrate conformity.
Why It Is Important: Timely and accurate filings demonstrate accountability and prevent penalties, invalid corporate actions, tax exposure, regulator concern and unreliable public or stakeholder information.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed where legislation, regulators, licences, standards, contracts or governance rules impose a form, content, frequency or deadline. Primary catalogue basis: ISO 37000; G20/OECD Principles; King IV. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Use a validated compliance calendar, controlled source data, reconciliation, maker-checker approval, authorized submission, official acknowledgement, exception handling and post-filing review. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Validate source, scope, form and deadline; identify data owners; reconcile source data; perform technical and Legal/Finance review as relevant; secure authorized approval; file before deadline; retain submitted version and official receipt; correct errors transparently; monitor changes. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Completed filing/return/register, source-data reconciliation, review checklist, approvals, submission log, official receipt, payment evidence, correspondence and correction record. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when the required item is complete, accurate, approved, submitted within the confirmed deadline and supported by an official acknowledgement and retained working papers. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes late/non-filing, inaccurate or incomplete data, unauthorized submission, missing payment, unsupported adjustment, absent official receipt or an outdated statutory register.
Typical Applicability / SBU: All legal entities and corporate offices

Why It Is Important: It protects accountability, lawful decision-making, shareholder interests and reliable oversight, and prevents unauthorized commitments or management override.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed to meet company law, governance codes, constitutional documents, board mandates and stakeholder expectations. Primary catalogue basis: ISO 37000; G20/OECD Principles; King IV. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Maintain approved governance bodies, charters, authority limits, meeting calendars, disclosures and decision records; route matters through authorized review and preserve an auditable trail. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Define applicable governance rules; assign board/management accountability; maintain approved charters and authority matrices; schedule required meetings and filings; declare conflicts; document decisions; monitor overdue actions and exceptions. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Approved charters, board/committee papers, agendas, minutes, resolutions, registers, declarations, authority approvals, filings and action-closure records. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when required governance actions occurred on time, by authorized persons, with complete approvals and records, and no unresolved mandatory governance breach remains. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes missing or late meetings/filings, unauthorized approval, undisclosed conflicts, incomplete statutory records, invalid delegations or unsupported decisions.
Typical Applicability / SBU: All legal entities and corporate offices

What It Is: Legal Register is the process for identifying, interpreting, implementing and monitoring binding legal and contractual obligations. Within Legal Compliance, it defines the obligation, accountable roles, control activities and evidence needed to demonstrate conformity.
Why It Is Important: It prevents unlawful activity, unenforceable commitments, penalties, disputes, licence loss and avoidable financial or reputational exposure.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed because each entity, transaction, contract, site and product is subject to laws, regulator directions, court orders and contractual commitments. Primary catalogue basis: ISO 37301. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Maintain a Legal-approved obligation register, matter and contract workflows, renewal/expiry controls, authorized advice, change monitoring, escalation and evidence retention. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Identify the exact source and applicability; obtain Legal approval; translate requirements into owned controls; review contracts and notices; track deadlines and renewals; manage disputes/orders; retain privileged and execution records; test compliance. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Legal register, applicability opinions, signed contracts, review checklists, approval records, notices, court/regulator correspondence, renewal alerts, matter logs and closure evidence. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when all applicable obligations are identified, legally validated, implemented, current, evidenced and tested without unresolved material breach. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes unidentified obligations, unapproved legal interpretations, expired commitments, missed orders/deadlines, unsigned or unauthorized contracts, uncontrolled notices or missing evidence.
Typical Applicability / SBU: All SBUs, entities, sites and contracts

Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Determine taxable scope and rates; configure master data; calculate from reconciled records; review exemptions and positions; obtain approval; file and pay on time; issue/retain required certificates; reconcile ledgers to returns; monitor audits and changes; remediate exceptions. Required Evidence: Registrations, tax computations, reconciliations, returns, challans/payment receipts, invoices, withholding certificates, customs declarations, transfer-pricing files, assessments, rulings and correspondence. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.

Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.

What It Is: Labour Law is the employment controls governing recruitment, contracts, pay, time, leave, benefits, conduct, welfare, performance and separation. Within Human Resource Compliance, it defines the obligation, accountable roles, control activities and evidence needed to demonstrate conformity.
Why It Is Important: It protects worker rights, workforce stability, fair treatment and payroll integrity while reducing disputes, penalties, buyer findings and operational disruption.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed under labour law/rules, wage orders, employment contracts, social-compliance standards and approved HR policies. Primary catalogue basis: ILO conventions; SA8000; Labour law. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Maintain lawful employment terms and worker records, accurate time/payroll, approved changes, grievance and disciplinary due process, welfare/safety interfaces, training and periodic compliance review. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Confirm worker classification and legal terms; issue contracts; verify age/right to work; record hours/leave; approve and pay wages/overtime/benefits accurately; prohibit discrimination/harassment/forced or child labour; manage grievances/discipline; control exits; retain records. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Personnel files, contracts, age/identity checks, attendance, overtime approvals, payroll and bank proof, leave/benefit records, grievance/discipline files, training, committee minutes and exit settlements. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when employment terms and practices match law/policy, payments and time records are accurate, rights are protected, cases follow due process and evidence covers the review period. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes child/forced labour, unpaid or late wages, excessive hours, unlawful deduction, harassment/discrimination, missing contract, inaccurate payroll, retaliation or unfair discipline/termination.
Typical Applicability / SBU: All employees, workers, contractors and workplaces

How It Should Work: Maintain lawful employment terms and worker records, accurate time/payroll, approved changes, grievance and disciplinary due process, welfare/safety interfaces, training and periodic compliance review. Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Confirm worker classification and legal terms; issue contracts; verify age/right to work; record hours/leave; approve and pay wages/overtime/benefits accurately; prohibit discrimination/harassment/forced or child labour; manage grievances/discipline; control exits; retain records. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Personnel files, contracts, age/identity checks, attendance, overtime approvals, payroll and bank proof, leave/benefit records, grievance/discipline files, training, committee minutes and exit settlements. Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when employment terms and practices match law/policy, payments and time records are accurate, rights are protected, cases follow due process and evidence covers the review period. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.

What It Is: ISO 45001 is the risk controls that prevent injury and occupational ill health and prepare the workplace for incidents and emergencies. Within Occupational Health & Safety, it defines the obligation, accountable roles, control activities and evidence needed to demonstrate conformity.
Why It Is Important: It protects life and health, preserves licence to operate, reduces downtime and demonstrates responsible control of hazardous work.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed under labour and fire law, BNBC/licence conditions, ISO 45001 and customer or insurance requirements. Primary catalogue basis: ISO 45001; ISO 45003. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Use hazard identification and risk assessment, hierarchy of controls, competent authorization, safe-work procedures, permits, equipment integrity, training, inspection, health surveillance, incident response and continual improvement. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Identify hazards; assess risk; eliminate/substitute where possible; engineer and administratively control residual risk; issue PPE; authorize high-risk work; train/verify competence; inspect and maintain; prepare/drill emergencies; report/investigate incidents; implement and retest CAPA. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Risk assessments, permits to work, LOTO records, training/competency, inspection and maintenance logs, PPE issue, medical surveillance, licences/NOCs, drill and incident reports, CAPA and trend data. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when hazards are controlled to approved levels, required permits/equipment/competence are current, activities are observed compliant and incidents/findings are effectively remediated. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes uncontrolled critical hazard, expired fire/safety approval, bypassed permit/LOTO, unsafe equipment, missing competence/PPE, unreported incident or overdue critical CAPA.
Typical Applicability / SBU: All factories, sites, offices and projects

Within Occupational Health & Safety, it defines the obligation, accountable roles, control activities and evidence needed to demonstrate conformity.
Why It Is Important: It protects life and health, preserves licence to operate, reduces downtime and demonstrates responsible control of hazardous work.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed under labour and fire law, BNBC/licence conditions, ISO 45001 and customer or insurance requirements. Primary catalogue basis: ISO 45001; ISO 45003. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Use hazard identification and risk assessment, hierarchy of controls, competent authorization, safe-work procedures, permits, equipment integrity, training, inspection, health surveillance, incident response and continual improvement. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Identify hazards; assess risk; eliminate/substitute where possible; engineer and administratively control residual risk; issue PPE; authorize high-risk work; train/verify competence; inspect and maintain; prepare/drill emergencies; report/investigate incidents; implement and retest CAPA. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Risk assessments, permits to work, LOTO records, training/competency, inspection and maintenance logs, PPE issue, medical surveillance, licences/NOCs, drill and incident reports, CAPA and trend data. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when hazards are controlled to approved levels, required permits/equipment/competence are current, activities are observed compliant and incidents/findings are effectively remediated. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes uncontrolled critical hazard, expired fire/safety approval, bypassed permit/LOTO, unsafe equipment, missing competence/PPE, unreported incident or overdue critical CAPA.

What It Is: ISO 14001 is the permit, impact and operational controls that prevent pollution and manage emissions, effluent, waste, resources, climate, water and biodiversity. Within Environmental Compliance, it defines the obligation, accountable roles, control activities and evidence needed to demonstrate conformity.
Why It Is Important: It protects communities and ecosystems, preserves licences and market access, reduces cleanup and resource costs, and supports credible sustainability commitments.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed under environmental law/rules, clearance conditions, ISO 14001, customer requirements and climate/nature reporting commitments. Primary catalogue basis: ISO 14001; ISO 14031. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Identify aspects and legal limits; maintain clearances; apply operational and engineering controls; monitor with calibrated methods; manage waste and contractors; report accurately; respond to incidents; review performance and CAPA. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Maintain an aspects/impacts and obligations register; hold valid clearance/permits; define limits and controls; operate treatment systems; sample/measure at required frequency; use competent labs; retain manifests and submissions; investigate exceedances; report/escalate; verify corrective action. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Clearance and conditions, aspect register, monitoring plan, lab reports, ETP/air/noise logs, calibration, waste manifests, contractor approvals, submissions, resource/GHG data, incident and CAPA records. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when authorizations are valid, limits and conditions are met throughout the period, data is complete and traceable, treatment/waste controls operate and exceptions are closed effectively. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes expired clearance, exceedance, uncontrolled discharge/emission, missing monitoring, falsified data, improper storage/disposal, unapproved contractor, unreported incident or unverified CAPA.
Typical Applicability / SBU: All sites with environmental aspects or permits

What It Is: Environmental Clearance is the lifecycle for obtaining, maintaining, renewing and complying with a required licence, permit, registration, certificate, clearance, NOC or approval. Within Environmental Compliance, it defines the obligation, accountable roles, control activities and evidence needed to demonstrate conformity.
Why It Is Important: A valid authorization can be a condition of lawful operation; failure may require shutdown, recall, seizure, penalty or regulator escalation.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed whenever a law, regulator, customer, certification scheme or site condition prohibits activity without prior or continuing approval. Primary catalogue basis: ISO 14001; ISO 14031. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Maintain a complete authorization register, named owner/deputy, condition tracker, 90/60/30/15/7/1-day reminders, maker-reviewer-approver workflow, renewal evidence and escalation that blocks unauthorized operation. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Confirm applicability and issuing authority; obtain approval before activity; record number, scope, conditions and expiry; monitor every condition; submit accurate renewal early; retain official receipt and certificate; escalate expiry; stop or restrict activity when authorization is absent unless written authority permits continuation. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Current certificate/permit/licence, application and fee receipt, regulator acknowledgement, approved conditions register, monitoring reports, inspection records, correspondence, renewal calendar and escalation logs. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when the authorization is valid for the correct entity/site/activity, every material condition is met, renewal is timely, official evidence is retained and the control operated throughout the period. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Non-compliant if approval is absent, expired, out of scope, condition-breached, obtained after activity without authority, renewed late, supported by inaccurate information or not evidenced.

Why It Is Needed: It is needed by ISO/IEC 27001/27002, cyber and privacy law, contracts, customer requirements and the organization's risk appetite. Primary catalogue basis: ISO/IEC 27001; ISO/IEC 27002. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Maintain asset and risk registers, security policies, role-based access, secure configuration, encryption, backup, logging, vulnerability/patch management, incident response, supplier controls, training and testing. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Classify assets/data; assess risk; assign owners; approve least-privilege access and MFA; harden/configure; encrypt and back up; log/monitor; patch vulnerabilities; test recovery; manage suppliers; train users; respond to incidents; review access and controls; retain evidence. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Asset/data registers, risk assessments, access requests/reviews, MFA/configuration reports, logs/SOC alerts, patch and vulnerability reports, backups/recovery tests, incidents, supplier assessments, training and audits. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when in-scope risks have effective controls, access/configuration/patching/backup and monitoring operate throughout the period, evidence is complete and incidents are resolved. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes unauthorized access, unsupported system, critical unpatched exposure, missing backup/test, disabled logging, uncontrolled privileged account, unreported incident, insecure supplier or missing evidence.
Typical Applicability / SBU: All information assets, systems and users

What It Is: NIST CSF is the operational controls that prevent, detect, contain, investigate and recover from cyber threats across endpoints, networks, cloud and applications. Within Cyber Security, it defines the obligation, accountable roles, control activities and evidence needed to demonstrate conformity.
Why It Is Important: It reduces business interruption, data loss, extortion, fraud and safety impact from increasingly capable and persistent threats.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed under cyber law, NIST CSF, CIS Controls, contracts, insurance conditions and accepted security practice. Primary catalogue basis: NIST CSF; CIS Controls; ISO/IEC 27001. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Identify assets and threats; protect through layered controls; continuously detect anomalies; respond using tested playbooks; recover from trusted backups; learn from incidents and threat intelligence. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Maintain inventory and criticality; secure identities/endpoints/networks/email/cloud; manage vulnerabilities and patches; monitor logs/alerts; test penetration and response; preserve forensic evidence; contain and notify incidents; recover and validate; track remediation. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Inventories, security architecture/configuration, EDR/SIEM reports, vulnerability and penetration tests, patch evidence, access/MFA reports, threat intelligence, incident/forensic records, recovery tests and CAPA. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when critical assets are covered by preventive/detective controls, high-risk vulnerabilities are timely resolved, monitoring and response are effective and recovery is tested. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes uncontrolled critical vulnerability, disabled protection/logging, compromised credentials, missed incident, untested recovery, unsupported asset, evidence loss or overdue high-risk remediation.
Typical Applicability / SBU: All digital infrastructure and connected operations

Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.

Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes activation before approval, hidden ownership, sanctions/PEP hit unresolved, sham qualification, inadequate enhanced review, missing clause, suspicious payment, overdue re-screening or ignored breach.

Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.

What It Is: Access Control is the layered protection of people, premises, warehouses, information and critical assets from unauthorized access, theft, sabotage and violence. Within Physical Security Compliance, it defines the obligation, accountable roles, control activities and evidence needed to demonstrate conformity.
Why It Is Important: It protects safety, inventory, confidential information and operational continuity and supports investigations and emergency response.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed by security risk assessment, insurance/customer requirements, ISO/IEC 27001 physical controls and site licences/contracts. Primary catalogue basis: ISO/IEC 27001 physical controls. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Assess site threats; define secure zones; control identities, badges, visitors, keys and vehicles; monitor CCTV/alarms/patrols; secure warehouses; manage guards; respond to incidents; retain and review logs. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Classify areas/assets; install proportionate perimeter/access controls; authorize and periodically review badges/keys; verify visitors/contractors; log entry; maintain CCTV/alarms/lighting; patrol; segregate high-value stock; train guards; test response; preserve footage/evidence; investigate and remediate. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Security assessment and plan, access/badge/key registers and reviews, visitor/vehicle logs, CCTV/alarms maintenance and footage requests, patrol/guard records, warehouse counts, incident reports and drill/CAPA evidence. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when access is authorized and traceable, critical zones/assets are protected and monitored, systems operate and incidents are promptly investigated and remediated. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes unauthorized entry, shared/unreturned badge/key, blind CCTV/disabled alarm, unlogged visitor, insecure stock, guard lapse, missing footage/evidence or repeated incident without CAPA.
Typical Applicability / SBU: All offices, factories, warehouses and projects

What It Is: Document Control is the controlled creation, identification, versioning, retention, protection, retrieval, legal hold, archiving and disposal of documents and records. Why It Is Important: It preserves reliable evidence, corporate memory and legal rights and prevents obsolete instructions, lost proof, privacy breach and improper destruction.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed by ISO 15489, legal limitation/retention duties, litigation holds, management-system standards, contracts and evidence requirements. Primary catalogue basis: ISO 15489; ISO 9001. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.

Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Classify documents/records; assign owner and retention; approve and version controlled documents; remove obsolete copies; protect confidentiality/integrity; index and retrieve; back up archives; suspend disposal for legal hold; authorize and evidence destruction; audit completeness. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Document master list, approved versions and change history, distribution/acknowledgement, records inventory, retention schedule, archive/index, access logs, legal holds, backup tests, disposal approvals/certificates and audits. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when current documents are available at point of use, required records are complete/retrievable/protected for the full period, holds override disposal and destruction is authorized and evidenced. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes obsolete instruction in use, missing/altered evidence, premature disposal, ignored legal hold, unauthorized access, expired retention without action, unrecoverable archive or undocumented destruction.

Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Approve product information and claims, control pricing/promotions, maintain complaint/warranty channels, investigate trends, communicate transparently, protect customer data and execute recall/correction when needed. What It Is: BSCI is the controls for identifying, implementing and evidencing binding buyer codes, audit protocols and customer-specific conditions. Within Buyer Compliance, it defines the obligation, accountable roles, control activities and evidence needed to demonstrate conformity.
Why It Is Important: Buyer compliance preserves market access and revenue and protects workers, product integrity and the customer's reputation.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed when contracts, purchase orders, approval programmes or certifications make a buyer code or audit scheme binding. Primary catalogue basis: BSCI; Sedex SMETA; WRAP; buyer codes. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Maintain a buyer-requirement matrix by site/product; assign owners; integrate requirements into HR/HSE/quality/supply-chain controls; keep authentic evidence; run readiness reviews; manage audits and CAPA; notify material change. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Obtain current buyer standard; determine site/product scope; map each requirement to control/owner/evidence; train relevant workers; prohibit falsification and coaching; self-assess; conduct worker-sensitive audits ethically; correct findings; verify CAPA; monitor certification/authorization expiry. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Current buyer code, contracts/POs, mapping matrix, training, worker and operational records, self-assessments, audit reports, FAMA/approval/certificates, CAPA and closure acceptance. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when every applicable buyer requirement is mapped and operating, records are authentic, audits/approvals are current and findings are accepted closed. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes expired approval, falsified record, unauthorized subcontracting, critical labour/safety breach, audit obstruction, undisclosed site, overdue finding or use outside buyer authorization.
Typical Applicability / SBU: Export and buyer-nominated supply chains

What It Is: Project Governance is the governance, control and assurance of temporary initiatives from approval through design, execution, commissioning and closure. Within Project Compliance, it defines the obligation, accountable roles, control activities and evidence needed to demonstrate conformity.
Why It Is Important: It protects investment, schedule, safety, quality and intended benefits and prevents unauthorized scope, cost, contractor or regulatory risk.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed by project governance, contracts, permits, ISO 21502/PMBOK/PRINCE2 and capital-approval requirements. Primary catalogue basis: ISO 21502; PMBOK; PRINCE2. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Use approved business case and stage gates, clear sponsor/accountability, integrated scope/schedule/cost/risk/quality/HSE controls, contractor governance, change control, commissioning and benefits/closure review. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Approve charter/business case and authority; identify requirements/permits; define scope and controls; plan resources/schedule/budget/risk; qualify contractors; manage design and HSE; control change and payment; inspect/test; commission with acceptance; hand over documents; close actions and lessons. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Charter/business case, approvals, requirement/permit register, plans and baselines, risk register, contracts, design reviews, HSE/quality records, progress/cost reports, changes, tests/commissioning, handover and closure review. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when the project remains within approved governance or authorized change, requirements and permits are met, deliverables pass acceptance and handover/closure evidence is complete. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes work before approval/permit, uncontrolled scope/cost, unqualified contractor, unsafe work, unapproved change/payment, failed acceptance, incomplete handover or unresolved critical defect.
Typical Applicability / SBU: Capital, construction, digital and transformation projects

What It Is: Circular Economy is the governance, due diligence, measurement and disclosure of material environmental, social and governance impacts, risks and commitments. Within Sustainability Compliance, it defines the obligation, accountable roles, control activities and evidence needed to demonstrate conformity.
Why It Is Important: It supports stakeholder trust, financing and buyer access and prevents misleading claims, unmanaged human-rights/climate risk and unreliable disclosures.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed by adopted GRI/ISSB/SASB standards, contracts, lender/buyer requirements, board commitments and applicable sustainability law. Primary catalogue basis: GRI; ISSB; ISO 14001; ISO 50001. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Conduct materiality and due diligence; define boundaries/methods; assign data owners; implement controls; monitor KPIs; address adverse impacts; reconcile and assure disclosures; approve claims; review progress and CAPA. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Identify applicable standards and stakeholders; assess material topics and impacts; set governance/policies/targets; map metrics and methodology; control source data and estimates; conduct human-rights/environmental due diligence; remediate impacts; review/approve disclosure; obtain assurance where required; prevent greenwashing. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Materiality and due-diligence records, policies/targets, metric dictionary, source data and calculations, GHG/water/social evidence, stakeholder engagement, remediation, review/approval, assurance and published report. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when scope and methods match the chosen framework, data is complete and traceable, material impacts are governed, claims are substantiated and disclosures pass review/assurance. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes omitted material topic, unsupported target/claim, inconsistent boundary, unreliable data, ignored adverse impact, greenwashing, missing approval or unresolved assurance finding.

Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Competition policy and training, pricing/bid analyses and approvals, competitor-contact register, meeting agendas/minutes, Legal contract advice, clean-team protocols, communications review and investigation/CAPA. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when decisions are demonstrably independent, high-risk agreements/contact receive Legal control, sensitive data is protected and no unresolved collusion or abuse indicator remains. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes price fixing, bid rigging, market/customer allocation, sensitive-data exchange, resale-price control, abusive exclusion, undocumented competitor meeting or ignored red flag.

Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.

Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.

Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.

Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when required tasks are current, critical backlog is controlled, condition remains acceptable, failures are analyzed and post-maintenance performance is verified. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes overdue critical maintenance, uncontrolled deferral, repeated failure without RCA, missing work evidence, wrong part/procedure, unsafe emergency repair or unverified return to service.

Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when every critical measurement uses suitable in-calibration equipment with traceable evidence and out-of-tolerance events are assessed and controlled. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes expired/unknown calibration, unsuitable accuracy, missing traceability, damaged/unidentified equipment, failed check ignored, unassessed prior results or altered certificate.

What It Is: Advertising Law is the legal and ethical control of advertising, promotions, digital campaigns, social media, brand use and customer targeting. Within Marketing Compliance, it defines the obligation, accountable roles, control activities and evidence needed to demonstrate conformity.
Why It Is Important: It protects consumers and brand trust and prevents misleading claims, privacy misuse, unfair promotions and unauthorized intellectual-property use.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed by consumer, competition, privacy, product and advertising rules, platform policies and brand/customer contracts. Primary catalogue basis: ICC Advertising Code; consumer and privacy law. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Use a campaign approval workflow with substantiation, Legal/product/privacy review, approved audience/data, terms and disclosures, brand/IP control, monitoring, complaint handling and record retention. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Document objective, audience and channels; substantiate every objective/green/health/performance claim; approve pricing and promotion terms; include required disclosures; verify consent and targeting; license content/brand; review influencers/agencies; approve before launch; monitor live content; correct complaints/errors; retain final creative and approvals. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Campaign brief, claim substantiation, Legal/technical/privacy approvals, promotion terms, consent/audience records, content/IP licences, agency/influencer agreements, final creative, platform records, monitoring, complaints and corrections. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when claims, targeting, terms and content are accurate, substantiated, approved and consistent in market, with privacy and complaint controls operating. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes misleading/unsubstantiated claim, undisclosed material term, invalid consent, prohibited targeting, unauthorized brand/content, unapproved influencer statement, live error not corrected or missing approval trail.

Why It Is Important: It protects revenue quality, competition and anti-bribery compliance and reduces channel misconduct, side agreements, bad debt and customer disputes.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed by sales and pricing policy, delegation of authority, competition/consumer/anti-bribery rules, contracts and credit requirements. Primary catalogue basis: ISO 37301; ISO 37001. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Approve customers/channels and credit; control price/discount/incentive authority; document contracts and commitments; screen high-risk parties; prevent side agreements; monitor returns/claims/payments; investigate anomalies. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Perform customer/dealer due diligence and credit review; approve pricing and discounts within authority; document incentives and objective criteria; Legal-review distribution restrictions; execute contract before supply; record orders/delivery/acceptance; reconcile rebates/returns; monitor suspicious patterns; renew/terminate channels properly. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: CDD/credit file, screening, approved price/discount/incentive, quotations/contracts, orders and delivery/acceptance, rebate/commission calculations, returns/claims, receivables, channel monitoring and exception approvals. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when counterparties and terms are approved, prices/incentives follow authority and law, transactions reconcile to contract and no undisclosed commitment or red flag remains. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes unauthorized discount/rebate, side agreement, fictitious sale, bribery-linked incentive, unapproved dealer, anti-competitive restriction, channel stuffing, unsupported return/commission or missing contract.

What It Is: Customer Due Diligence is the risk-based onboarding, due diligence, contracting, monitoring and offboarding of suppliers, agents, dealers, distributors, contractors and other associates. Within Sales Compliance, it defines the obligation, accountable roles, control activities and evidence needed to demonstrate conformity.
Why It Is Important: Third parties can create bribery, sanctions, labour, quality, cyber, environmental and reputation exposure for the organization.

Primary catalogue basis: ISO 37301; ISO 37001. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.

Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Define risk criteria; identify beneficial owners; collect and verify documents; screen and investigate red flags; conduct enhanced due diligence for high risk; approve independently; contract required controls/audit rights; train as needed; monitor performance/payments; re-screen; suspend/terminate when risk is unacceptable. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.

Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.

What It Is: Letter of Credit is the legal and documentary controls for importing, exporting, classifying, valuing, licensing, financing and shipping goods or technology across borders. Within Export Customer Compliance, it defines the obligation, accountable roles, control activities and evidence needed to demonstrate conformity.
Why It Is Important: It protects market access and revenue and prevents seizure, penalty, sanctions violation, customs debt, delay and false trade documentation.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed under customs/import-export law, policy orders, sanctions/export-control regimes, letters of credit, Incoterms and customer/country rules. Primary catalogue basis: Incoterms 2020; UCP 600. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Classify products and parties; validate licences/restrictions/origin/value; screen destinations; prepare accurate documents; authorize declarations; reconcile duties and shipments; retain records; audit brokers and changes. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Maintain product/HS master and rationale; verify import/export registration and permits; screen parties/countries/goods; establish origin and valuation; approve Incoterms/LC terms; issue consistent invoice/packing/shipping documents; review broker declaration; pay/reconcile duties; retain proof; correct errors. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Licences/registrations, classification worksheets/rulings, screening, origin certificates, valuation support, contracts/LC, invoices, packing lists, declarations, bills of lading, duty payment and broker correspondence. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when every shipment is authorized, correctly classified/valued, unsanctioned, accurately documented, duties/conditions are met and records reconcile end to end. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes prohibited trade, wrong HS/value/origin, expired licence, false document, inconsistent shipment records, unapproved destination, sanctions hit, unpaid duty or unsupported correction.

What It Is: Tender Integrity is the risk-based controls that prevent, detect and respond to bribery and corruption involving employees, officials and third parties. Within Procurement Integrity, it defines the obligation, accountable roles, control activities and evidence needed to demonstrate conformity.
Why It Is Important: It prevents criminal and civil exposure, protects tender and commercial integrity, and reduces financial, debarment and reputation risk.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed by anti-corruption law, ISO 37001, contractual commitments and the expectation that organizations control associates acting on their behalf. Primary catalogue basis: ISO 37001; ISO 37301. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Perform bribery-risk assessment and due diligence; control gifts, hospitality, donations, sponsorship, facilitation payments and third parties; apply financial/commercial controls; train, monitor, investigate and remediate. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Approve anti-bribery policy and risk assessment; identify high-risk roles/transactions; conduct proportionate due diligence before engagement; include clauses; apply segregation and payment controls; maintain registers; provide reporting channels; investigate; test and review. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Risk assessments, due-diligence files, screening, contracts, COI/gifts registers, approvals, invoices/payment support, training, monitoring results, investigation and CAPA records. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when high-risk relationships and transactions receive complete pre-approval and due diligence, controls operate, red flags are resolved and no prohibited payment or unresolved allegation remains. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes facilitation payment, improper benefit, sham invoice, unapproved high-risk agent, ignored red flag, inadequate due diligence, off-book record, retaliation or ineffective investigation.
Typical Applicability / SBU: Tenders, supplier selection and awards

What It Is: AI Governance is the governance of artificial-intelligence systems and models across intake, design, data, testing, deployment, monitoring and retirement. Within Artificial Intelligence Compliance, it defines the obligation, accountable roles, control activities and evidence needed to demonstrate conformity.
Why It Is Important: It reduces unfair, unsafe, opaque, insecure or unreliable automated decisions and protects people, data, operations and trust.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed by ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF, privacy/cyber/product/employment obligations and management accountability for automated decisions. Primary catalogue basis: ISO/IEC 42001; NIST AI RMF. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Maintain an AI inventory and risk classification; define accountable owner and human oversight; assess data and impact; validate performance, bias, robustness and security; approve deployment; monitor drift/incidents; manage vendors and change; preserve traceability. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Register each use case/model; document purpose, users and prohibited use; assess legal/ethical/safety/privacy/security impact; control data provenance/quality; define human review and appeal; test performance/bias/robustness; independently approve high risk; document model/version; monitor drift/outcomes; log incidents; revalidate change; retire safely. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: AI inventory, use-case and impact assessments, data/model cards, provenance, test and bias results, risk acceptance, human-oversight procedure, approvals, vendor evidence, monitoring/drift logs, decisions, incidents and change/retirement records. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when the use case is approved for its actual purpose, risks and data are controlled, tests meet defined thresholds, human oversight works, outputs are monitored and change is traceable. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes unregistered AI, prohibited/unlawful use, unknown data provenance, material bias/error, no human appeal, insecure model, drift ignored, undocumented change, vendor opacity or deployment before approval.
Typical Applicability / SBU: AI systems, vendors, models and automated decisions

What It Is: Supply Chain ESG is the governance, due diligence, measurement and disclosure of material environmental, social and governance impacts, risks and commitments. Within ESG Due Diligence, it defines the obligation, accountable roles, control activities and evidence needed to demonstrate conformity.
Why It Is Important: It supports stakeholder trust, financing and buyer access and prevents misleading claims, unmanaged human-rights/climate risk and unreliable disclosures.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed by adopted GRI/ISSB/SASB standards, contracts, lender/buyer requirements, board commitments and applicable sustainability law. Primary catalogue basis: UN Guiding Principles; OECD Due Diligence Guidance. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Conduct materiality and due diligence; define boundaries/methods; assign data owners; implement controls; monitor KPIs; address adverse impacts; reconcile and assure disclosures; approve claims; review progress and CAPA. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Identify applicable standards and stakeholders; assess material topics and impacts; set governance/policies/targets; map metrics and methodology; control source data and estimates; conduct human-rights/environmental due diligence; remediate impacts; review/approve disclosure; obtain assurance where required; prevent greenwashing. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Materiality and due-diligence records, policies/targets, metric dictionary, source data and calculations, GHG/water/social evidence, stakeholder engagement, remediation, review/approval, assurance and published report. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when scope and methods match the chosen framework, data is complete and traceable, material impacts are governed, claims are substantiated and disclosures pass review/assurance. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes omitted material topic, unsupported target/claim, inconsistent boundary, unreliable data, ignored adverse impact, greenwashing, missing approval or unresolved assurance finding.
Typical Applicability / SBU: Suppliers, investments, acquisitions and major projects

What It Is: Crisis Response is the preparedness, response, continuity and recovery arrangements for disruptive incidents and crises. Within Crisis Management, it defines the obligation, accountable roles, control activities and evidence needed to demonstrate conformity.
Why It Is Important: It protects people, critical services, customers, revenue and reputation and enables controlled recovery within acceptable time and data-loss limits.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed by ISO 22301/22320, customer and lender commitments, insurance conditions and governance expectations for resilience. Primary catalogue basis: ISO 22301; ISO 22320. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Identify critical activities and dependencies; set approved RTO/RPO; maintain continuity, crisis communication and disaster-recovery plans; provision resources; exercise scenarios; track lessons and CAPA. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Complete business impact and risk assessments; identify dependencies/alternatives; approve strategies and plans; define command and communications; maintain contacts/resources; back up critical data; train teams; exercise and recover; measure objectives; remediate gaps; review after change/incidents. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: BIA and risk assessment, continuity/DR/crisis plans, RTO/RPO approvals, contact trees, backup/recovery evidence, exercise reports, incident logs, communications, lessons learned and CAPA. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when critical scope and objectives are approved, plans/resources are current, exercises demonstrate recovery within objectives and identified gaps are closed and retested. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes missing critical process, obsolete plan/contact, untested recovery, failed RTO/RPO, unavailable backup/resource, confused authority, communication failure or overdue exercise CAPA.

Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Identify hazards; assess risk; eliminate/substitute where possible; engineer and administratively control residual risk; issue PPE; authorize high-risk work; train/verify competence; inspect and maintain; prepare/drill emergencies; report/investigate incidents; implement and retest CAPA. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Risk assessments, permits to work, LOTO records, training/competency, inspection and maintenance logs, PPE issue, medical surveillance, licences/NOCs, drill and incident reports, CAPA and trend data. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when hazards are controlled to approved levels, required permits/equipment/competence are current, activities are observed compliant and incidents/findings are effectively remediated. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes uncontrolled critical hazard, expired fire/safety approval, bypassed permit/LOTO, unsafe equipment, missing competence/PPE, unreported incident or overdue critical CAPA.

Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.

Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.

How It Should Work: Assess site threats; define secure zones; control identities, badges, visitors, keys and vehicles; monitor CCTV/alarms/patrols; secure warehouses; manage guards; respond to incidents; retain and review logs. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Classify areas/assets; install proportionate perimeter/access controls; authorize and periodically review badges/keys; verify visitors/contractors; log entry; maintain CCTV/alarms/lighting; patrol; segregate high-value stock; train guards; test response; preserve footage/evidence; investigate and remediate. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Security assessment and plan, access/badge/key registers and reviews, visitor/vehicle logs, CCTV/alarms maintenance and footage requests, patrol/guard records, warehouse counts, incident reports and drill/CAPA evidence. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when access is authorized and traceable, critical zones/assets are protected and monitored, systems operate and incidents are promptly investigated and remediated. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes unauthorized entry, shared/unreturned badge/key, blind CCTV/disabled alarm, unlogged visitor, insecure stock, guard lapse, missing footage/evidence or repeated incident without CAPA.

What It Is: Business Travel is the employment controls governing recruitment, contracts, pay, time, leave, benefits, conduct, welfare, performance and separation. Within Travel & Mobility Compliance, it defines the obligation, accountable roles, control activities and evidence needed to demonstrate conformity.
Why It Is Important: It protects worker rights, workforce stability, fair treatment and payroll integrity while reducing disputes, penalties, buyer findings and operational disruption.
Why It Is Needed: It is needed under labour law/rules, wage orders, employment contracts, social-compliance standards and approved HR policies. Primary catalogue basis: ISO 31030; immigration and tax law. Applicability must be validated for the specific SBU, entity, site, product, activity and jurisdiction.
How It Should Work: Maintain lawful employment terms and worker records, accurate time/payroll, approved changes, grievance and disciplinary due process, welfare/safety interfaces, training and periodic compliance review. Link the source → obligation → risk → control → owner → due date → evidence → testing → finding/CAPA → management review.
Minimum Requirements for Compliance: Confirm worker classification and legal terms; issue contracts; verify age/right to work; record hours/leave; approve and pay wages/overtime/benefits accurately; prohibit discrimination/harassment/forced or child labour; manage grievances/discipline; control exits; retain records. Universal CMS controls: assign a unique ID; document applicability and source; obtain Legal approval for legal interpretations; name owner/reviewer/approver; define frequency and due date; prevent closure without evidence; retain audit trail; escalate exceptions; complete CAPA and independent effectiveness retest.
Required Evidence: Personnel files, contracts, age/identity checks, attendance, overtime approvals, payroll and bank proof, leave/benefit records, grievance/discipline files, training, committee minutes and exit settlements. Evidence must be authentic, current, attributable, approved where required, protected and retrievable.
Audit / Pass Criteria: Pass only when employment terms and practices match law/policy, payments and time records are accurate, rights are protected, cases follow due process and evidence covers the review period. A COMPLIANT conclusion requires both effective design and effective operation, current sufficient evidence for the full in-scope period, and no unresolved mandatory or critical/high breach. Missing material evidence means NOT DEMONSTRATED, not compliant.
Non-Compliance Triggers: Failure includes child/forced labour, unpaid or late wages, excessive hours, unlawful deduction, harassment/discrimination, missing contract, inaccurate payroll, retaliation or unfair discipline/termination.
Typical Applicability / SBU: Business travel, expatriates and international assignments
